analysis:
All four units are documentation-only changes: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 557-564 are the substantive delta; the rest is unchanged context) and docs/architecture/inference.md (new shape-warmup paragraphs, patch hunk @@ -977,6 +977,54). No executable code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation or authorization logic is modified, so TB-002, TB-009 and TB-011 and the T-053 binding/revocation boundaries are not altered by this PR.

The documentation describes a startup shape warmup that runs excluded probes and cells on a loaded engine. Documented properties relevant to the threat model: it uses synthetic prompts (no consumer data, so A-001 is not touched); it publishes no rates or work totals; it runs inside the same KV and service budgets and the same idle gate and foreground lease (customer requests preempt it); and it has a 20 s wall budget. Its startup-preload pass runs before registration and does not touch the registration or attestation path, other than the registration gate's timeout, which still bounds it. Related availability points (T-010, T-029, T-057) are unaffected. The doc also says the periodic MLX pool sweep defers while a calibration session runs, but on-pressure reclaims still run. If the code diverges from this description, the pressure-reclaim path could be a minor availability question. The supplied evidence is only documentation and cannot confirm the code.

The cache residue relevant to T-041 is unchanged: the warmup creates no prefix-cache donations as described, and the docs make no change to TTL, HMAC naming or salt scoping. A residual question for the integration pass is whether the warmup's synthetic prompts could be donated to or hit the SSD prefix cache. The docs do not say, and the code is not supplied; this is low risk because the entries would carry no tenant data.

No regression, invalidated assumption or threat-model gap was identified from these docs. The inference.md patch excerpt is truncated, so a few trailing sentences are only visible via the shown portion.
